correctness.rationale: For \(k>0\), the two vertex conditions force \(\sin(k\ell)=0\), so the positive spectrum is exactly \((m\pi/\ell)^2\). Each level splits into a symmetric cosine line and an \(N-1\)-dimensional sine coefficient space \(\mathbf1^\perp\). On any fixed edge, the squared supremum is the quadratic coefficient norm because a phase interval of length \(m\pi\) contains a full absolute maximum. Taking the trace over any orthonormal eigenspace basis gives \(2/(N\ell)+2(1-1/N)/\ell=2/\ell\). The zero mode contributes \(1/(N\ell)\), yielding the claimed exact series and constant strict gap. The attached verifier checks the projector algebra and numerical heat sums but is not used as a substitute for the infinite analytic proof.

value.rationale: This is not a free-standing recomputation of a familiar spectrum: it answers a concrete conjectural comparison introduced for eigenfunction localization, on an infinite natural family of highly degenerate quantum graphs. The identity reveals the structural reason for strictness: every positive-frequency edgewise \(L^\infty\)-weight exactly matches a decoupled Neumann edge despite \(N\)-fold degeneracy, so topology enters the envelope only through the zero-mode deficit \((N-1)/(N\ell)\). That exact cancellation is directly useful when the envelope is inserted into Harrell–Maltsev eigenfunction bounds and supplies a sharp benchmark for extensions to unequal pumpkins and other symmetric graphs.
